label: Time symmetries of a history preserve giving being
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, attribution deferred (time symmetry of giving; the contrastive principle of sufficient reason applied to moments): in every history v of the model, if an order automorphism sigma of the times preserves every being's presence and every supplied non-giving time-indexed fact (PreservesHistory, definition 6d0f77a2), then for all g, x and t, g gives x being at t iff g gives x being at sigma t (GivesAt, definition 158301bc). Meaning: where nothing in the history's presence pattern and supplied facts distinguishes two moments, nothing distinguishes giving at one from giving at the other. Shape of Leibniz's argument that, were time distinct from things, no reason could be given why things are applied to some instants rather than others (2bd8f0e3, sourced; uniform space 7dd2af35); applying it to the schedule of giving is the analyst's. Recorded rivals: Clarke's reply that a will may choose without an external difference (81ec01fe), a free giver at one arbitrary moment (Control part 2), and noncontrastive, intrinsic or probabilistic explanation that leaves alternatives (e35adb5f). Leibniz himself draws from the temporal argument that instants without things are nothing, which presses against the possibility of distinct indiscernible moments that the price analysis in docs/notes/ca-horizontal-support.md assumes. Its warrant is a contrastive PSR, not 40a97664: it holds in every inertial interpretation with no giving (parts 1 and 3) and in begun inertia with giving at onset only (part 4), where an automorphism preserving the begun thing's presence fixes its first moment (checked for that control). As typed it is stronger than a contrastive principle in two ways: it is relative to the supplied Facts, which must not encode giving, so an incomplete Facts lets a map move unsupplied facts; and it does not require the history's designated present moment (History.now) to be preserved.
